summary.headline: Shanti Gold Q4 FY26 revenue rose 121.65% YoY to INR 658.93 crore, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin at 10.17%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 658.93 crore, up 121.65% YoY, the highest quarterly revenue in company history, driven by new customers, higher volumes and elevated gold prices. FY26 revenue reached INR 2,018.71 crore (+82.46%), with PAT of INR 140.15 crore (6.94% margin). Management changed inventory valuation from FIFO to weighted average cost with retrospective effect from April 1, 2024. Much of the profit uplift was attributed by management to inventory gains from gold bought outright with IPO proceeds, and management guided to a core PAT margin of around 4%.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 9.19 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Studded / bridal jewellery (existing line)
segments.commentary: Management said about 70% of revenue comes from the existing studded line; bridal jewellery carries higher margins and contributed to the Q4 EBITDA improvement.

segments.name: Plain gold jewellery (new line)
segments.commentary: About 30% of revenue is from the newly entered machine-made plain gold segment, which management described as lower margin, higher volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: volume growth of 30% to 40% and value growth of 60% to 70%; management cited FY27 turnover of around INR 3,000 to 3,500 crore in one answer and about INR 4,000 crore in another.

Core PAT margin guided at around 4% (management cited a 3.5% to 4% core range); the FY26 margin above this was attributed to inventory gains on gold bought outright with IPO proceeds, which management says is now mitigated and not included in guidance.
Export share guided to rise from about 5-10% to 10-20% this year, with Dubai subsidiary incorporation extended to June 2026.
Management expects to reach full 7,900 kg capacity in three to four years.
Working capital: management said inventory and trade receivables are each under 50 days; plain jewellery is expected to improve working capital cycle over time.
Debt-equity: management said it is comfortable at up to 1:1 (currently 0.36) to fund growth.
capex_capacity: Existing Andheri facility: installed capacity about 2,700 kg per annum, operating at around 65% utilisation.
Marol facility in Mumbai: adds about 4,000 kg per annum; management said it should be ready in about a month, starting at roughly 100 kg per month before ramping up.
Jaipur facility: adds 1,200 kg per annum; expected to start around September-October 2026.
Post-expansion total installed capacity is about 7,900 kg per annum, roughly three times the current capacity.
Quarterly volume reported at about 145-150 kg per month in a Q&A answer, which management said was disclosed quarterly in the presentation.
demand_pricing: Management said the structural shift from unorganised to organised jewellery retail is driving outsourcing to scalable manufacturers.

Management said demand is resilient, particularly in wedding and occasion-led categories; new products include Turkish jewellery (Turkish artisans onboarded for Marol), Mangalsutra and Cuban bracelets.
Management said the company has more than 400 customers and about 7% of volume or value from its top customer; it does not supply Titan/Tanishq currently.

Gold price context: management cited a move from about INR 78,000 to about INR 108,000 per 10 g and an assumed price of about INR 1,50,000 for guidance; it said guidance is based on current prices and not speculation.
Management said the 15% import duty increase would not hurt demand, citing a period when duty was 15% for many years and was cut to 6% last year.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY26 growth mainly price-driven, and what is the demand outlook ex-gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume grew about 15% in FY26 after the IPO and value growth was higher; FY27 is guided at 30-40% volume and 60-70% value growth.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable margin and how much of FY26 profit was from gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a core PAT margin of around 4% is sustainable; the extra profit came from gold bought outright with IPO money, when gold prices rose.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and volume per month?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is about 65%; volume is about 145-150 kg per month per the quarterly figures in the presentation.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and maximum debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-equity of up to 1:1 is the target ceiling, with the current ratio at 0.36; inventory and receivables are each under 50 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volume guidance fall from 60-70% to 30-40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 volume grew 15% and FY27 guidance of 40% plus is an increase, not a reduction; no contradiction in volume guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging policy and inventory held?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its hedging policy is to buy as it sells; it said about 600 kg of stock plus debtors is left, and it does not chase price movements.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility: management acknowledged gains and losses from inventory price movements; FY26 profit included inventory gains that management says are now excluded from guidance.
Margin gap: FY26 PAT margin was 6.94% versus the 4% core margin guided for FY27, and an analyst noted that doubling revenue to INR 4,000 crore at 4% implies only about INR 160 crore PAT.
Execution of the Marol (about 4,000 kg) and Jaipur (1,200 kg) ramp-ups, and the timing of the Jaipur start in September-October 2026.
Working capital and receivables: debtor days rose from 42 to 48-49; management expects new plain jewellery to improve the cycle.
Leverage: debt-equity expected to rise towards 1:1 to fund growth from 0.36 currently.
Geopolitical risk: the Dubai subsidiary has been delayed to June 2026 and export share targets depend on it.
Management said the 15% import duty would not hurt demand, but the duty increase is a demand-side watch item.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and demand, but defensive and at times evasive on margin sustainability and gold-price exposure, repeatedly redirecting to a 4% core margin. Answers on the inventory gains and PAT trajectory were inconsistent, and the call was marked by answers that were brief and sometimes unclear.
key_quotes: Q4FY26, we achieved the highest ever quarterly revenues in the histo ry of the company, reflecting our strong execution capabilities, improving scales, and increased relevance as a trusted manufacturing partner for organized jewellers.
We are not speculating on the gold market price movement whether it goes North or South.
So our core margin, come what may, will always remain between in the range of 3.4% to 4%, which is the normal industry range.
Our hedging policy is quite simple. We buy as we sell. Simple.

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 60-70% value growth and 30-40% volume growth is backed by Marol (4,000 kg/yr, ready in about a month) and Jaipur (1,200 kg/yr, Sep-Oct 2026) capacity additions, with current utilisation at 65%; however, the brief's FY27 turnover figures conflict (INR 3,000-3,500 crore vs ~4,000 crore), and the FY26 profit uplift was partly inventory gains.
